Empirical Research Plan  
“Investment Behavior of Private vs. Public Natural-Gas Firms”

------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study extension.

Rationale  
• We observe the same firms before and after a clearly-dated regulatory change.  
• The regulation altered the cost/benefit of investment more for one group (public firms) than for the other (private firms), creating cross-sectional treatment intensity.  
• We have panel data with multiple pre- and post-years, allowing firm and year fixed effects that soak up time-invariant firm heterogeneity and common macro shocks.  
• An event-study (dynamic DID) allows us to test the parallel-trend assumption and visualise the effect path.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treat_it = 1 if firm i is PUBLIC × year t is in Post-Policy period, 0 otherwise.

Control group  
• Primary counterfactual: PRIVATE firms in all years (they face no or minimal change).  
• Secondary within-public control (robustness): PUBLIC firms operating in regulatory jurisdictions exempt from the change.

Treatment timing / event date  
Policy announced: 2014-Q4  
Policy implemented: 2015-01-01  
We code Post_t = 1 for fiscal years ending 2015 or later.

No RDD running variable is required.

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In absence of the policy, investment by public and private firms would have evolved similarly.  
Plausibility: Same input markets and cyclical exposure; we will examine pre-trend plots and placebo tests.

A2. No differential anticipation: Firms did not alter investment before 2014-Q4 based on foreknowledge.  
Plausibility: The rule was proposed and finalised quickly; trade press indicates surprise.

A3. Stable composition: No massive switching between private/public status that is itself caused by the policy.  
Plausibility: Going public is lengthy; we will drop firms that switch status during sample as robustness.

A4. No contemporaneous shocks that differentially hit public firms exactly at 2015 (e.g., listing-specific tax changes).  
Plausibility: We will include industry-sub-segment × year FE and macro controls; search news to document no such shocks.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Different pre-trends (violates A1)  
• Mitigation: Event-study coefficients (k = –5,…,–1). If statistically flat, pre-trends satisfied. If not, adopt Propensity-Score-Reweighted DID (Abadie 2005) or synthetic-control style weights.

T2. Selection into public status around the event (violates A3)  
• Mitigation: Freeze treatment status at 2013 values; drop IPOs 2014–2016; perform robustness restricting to firms continuously public/private 2010–2020.

T3. Spillovers: Policy indirectly changes private‐firm investment through input-price shifts.  
• Mitigation: (i) Measure local input prices and control for them; (ii) Triple-difference: public vs private × affected vs unaffected jurisdictions × pre/post.

------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # high-dimensional FE regressions
library(did)          # Callaway-Sant’Anna estimators
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load Data
gas <- fread("natural_gas_firm_panel.csv")  # firm_id, year, investment, assets, public, etc.

# 2. Variable Construction
gas[, post := ifelse(year >= 2015, 1, 0)]
gas[, treat := public * post]                   # DID interaction
gas[, lninvest := log(investment + 1)]          # outcome
gas[, lnassets := log(total_assets)]

# 3. Main DID Specification
did_main <- feols(lninvest ~ treat + post + public + lnassets + profitability,
                  data = gas,
                  fixef = ~ firm_id + year,
                  cluster = "firm_id")
summary(did_main)

# 4. Event-Study (±5 years)
gas[, rel_year := year - 2015]                 # 0 = first treated year
es <- feols(lninvest ~ i(rel_year, public, ref = -1) + lnassets + profitability |
            firm_id + year,
            data = gas[rel_year >= -5 & rel_year <= 5],
            cluster = "firm_id")
iplot(es, main = "Event Study: Public vs Private Investment")

# 5. Robustness Check: Drop switchers
stable <- gas[!(switcher)]                     # define switcher earlier
did_stable <- update(did_main, data = stable)
etable(list(Main = did_main, NoSwitch = did_stable))
```

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------
Theory: Public firms have superior capital-market access but may face greater short-termism. When regulation lowered financing frictions mainly for public firms, I expect:

• Direction: Public firms increase investment relative to private firms.  
• Magnitude: Roughly +2–3 p.p. of CAPEX-to-Assets ratio (≈10–15 % increase over pre-policy mean for publics).

------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
(Coded 1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)
------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Parallel pre-trends visually and statistically supported ………… 0.8  
C2: No anticipatory behaviour/announcement effects …………………… 0.7  
C3: No time-varying confounders correlated with treatment ……… 0.6  
C4: Stable unit composition/no treatment reassignment ……………… 0.8  
C5: No spillovers/contamination across groups …………………………… 0.6  

Average score = 0.7 → “good but not bullet-proof”; event-study, triple-diff, and robustness checks are essential.
